properties.name: Behind a trusted gateway, the gateway names the design's owner and each caller's seat
properties.rationale: Owner's word, Anthony 2026-10-30: "Yes, fix the three flo2.io findings (the chat connector names the first read, flo2 records each design's owner, each caller gets their own seat in the cue counts)." Engine causes, measured on the published 0.94.0: fact:root-cause-behind-a-trusted-gateway-the-engine-can-learn-a-designs-owner-only-from-owned-by-2026-10-30 and fact:root-cause-the-usage-ledger-takes-its-seat-from-the-mcp-session-so-a-gateways-callers-share-one-2026-10-30; the gateway halves are in flo2's design (1a97fc1f1de4d5d2). CLASS: who is calling was the trusted host's word per call (writes_for), but who OWNS the design and which caller a ledger line is were still read from the design and the transport. The fix gives the host the same per-call route for both, and only behind a declared trusted gateway (a local caller or a bearer token's holder could otherwise name themselves owner or wear another's seat). WHY NOT A BACKFILL of OWNED_BY into stored designs: it would write into people's designs. WHY NOT ONE ENGINE SESSION PER CALLER: a store's open files each, 64 designs open at most. Both new tests FAILED with the two lines disabled (owner word forced off; ledger seat forced to the session's) and pass at d09ee3830; dev-test plus on_disk 3773 passed, 0 failed; clippy and fmt clean. LIMITS: claim_region still takes its seat as an argument; the handshake's instructions offer is still recorded on the gateway's own session seat, so behind flo2.io it reads unattributable. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Two per-call _meta keys a trusted gateway may send, honoured only under --http-trusted-gateway (CallerRule::host_names_owner_and_seat) and ignored everywhere else: reflow2/design_owners (Contributor ids; the settling cue's owner check, call_can_give_the_owners_word, reads them in place of the design's OWNED_BY; nothing is written; a hub's view does not hand them on to a member) and reflow2/seat (the caller's seat, written on the call's usage-ledger line in place of the session's, so cues::tally follows cues per caller over one shared engine session). New DESIGN_OWNERS task-local beside WRITES_FOR (accounted for in no_per_design_process_globals). AGENTS.md names both keys; changelog.d fragment the-gateway-names-the-owner-and-each-callers-seat.md. No tool, argument or reply schema changes.
